reasoning: Kasra then long aa: mishwaar. Covers an errand, a short trip and an outing, as the English says.
bil-marra is the Palestinian at all; the verb negates with ما and keeps the b-prefix, bi3raf for he knows. Taa marbuta after ر is a.
Dual of مرحبا with the Palestinian -een ending. The warm reply to mar7aba.
haad is the Palestinian this. ي is a moon letter so the article stays il-. حلو is 7ilu with a final u.
Taa marbuta after ج is e. The temperature sense is normal: 3ishriin daraje.
ث is a plain t in Palestinian, so respelled متل. As a noun with this meaning it is a proverb; as a particle mitl means like.
Long oo then final a: kuusa. The collective for the pale courgettes used in kuusa ma7shi.
Feminine participle raay7a, used for the immediate future. The pharyngeal ح keeps the taa marbuta as a.
muu is Syrian and north Lebanese negation. A Ramallah speaker says mish; the row's own label as a northern variant is accurate.
7atta plus a bare subjunctive for purpose. khallaS has shadda on ل and an emphatic S; bakiir is the Palestinian early.
The short counting form used before a noun, arba3 iyyaam; the free-standing number is arba3a.
Relative اللي with the 3ms b-present twice. The initial short vowel of yi3raf drops after the prefix: bi3raf.
Palestinian voices the ت to d and glottalises the ق, giving burd'aan, so the Arabic is respelled بردقان. burtu'aan is the more careful variant.

meaning_fix: machine / device / tool; a musical instrument is aale muusiiqiyye
reasoning: Initial آ is the long vowel aa, and the taa marbuta after ل comes out as e. On its own the word means a machine or device, not specifically an instrument.
Political register, but thawra and thaar 3ala are genuinely said in Ramallah, where this learned word keeps its ث. Everyday speech would otherwise say 'aam 3ala.
Taa marbuta becomes -it in a construct: faatuurit. كهربا loses the final hamza of MSA كهرباء in Palestinian.
ذ has no interdental in urban Palestinian and this native word takes d, so respelled دوقك; the ق is a glottal stop. Said to return a compliment.
Italian loan with a long ee in the stressed syllable: baazeela. The standard Palestinian word for peas.
ra7 is the Palestinian future particle before a bare verb, and fii is the existential there is. Taa marbuta after ل is e.
English loan kept close to the source, with a long ee in the last syllable. Some speakers end it with a v, maykroweev.
Long oo, not uu: yoom. Plural is iyyaam.
ط is emphatic T. Taa marbuta after ب is e: ruTuube.
Form II participle with shadda on ش, which doubles the whole digraph. ana mrashsha7 is the normal way to say I have a cold.
biddi plus a bare subjunctive. طاولة is Taawle with an emphatic T and e for the taa marbuta after ل.
إذا is said iza in urban Palestinian, hence the respelling. The 3ms of إجا in the b-present is biiji.
